methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $10M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Chips & Semiconductors (found 0 same-stage, 1 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 11 same-sector peers exist in Chips & Semiconductors, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Lab 91 is a Seed-stage semiconductor company founded by Anand Chamarthy that has raised $10M+. The valuation analysis draws on a sector universe of 11 private peers in Chips & Semiconductors, including well-known names such as Cerebras, SambaNova Systems, and Tenstorrent, alongside three public comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD).

Stage-progression methodology is the primary applicable triangulation approach. Using the $10M total capital raised as a proxy for current valuation and applying a 2.5x multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $25M. A peer-median approach was not feasible due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables in the narrow Chips & Semiconductors category; while 11 same-sector peers exist, fewer than three met the filtering criteria needed for reliable median benchmarking.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $21M to $29M, with a median point of $25M. This range reflects the single-method triangulation and assumes stable execution through Series A. Key uncertainties include the early-stage nature of the company, the concentration of evidence on stage-progression progression alone, and the limited availability of tightly comparable peers at identical developmental stages in frontier semiconductor infrastructure. Refinement of this range would benefit from expanded peer data or additional financial metrics as the company matures.
